title: Private: ship signed policy bundle artifact + upgrade docs
author: Fatima Noor
body:
Context: Private (VPC/on-prem, including air-gapped) needs an auditable, tamper-evident way to distribute RBAC v2 policy bundles. Today we mostly rely on “drop a directory of YAML/JSON on disk” patterns, which are hard to reason about for upgrades and provide no integrity guarantees.

This PR adds:
- A signed, deterministic policy bundle artifact format intended for Redwood Private deployments.
- A small packaging/verifier CLI that produces and verifies the artifact.
- Documentation for how bundles are updated during Private upgrades and how version skew is handled.

What ships (artifact):
- Output is a single tar.gz: rbac-policy-bundle-<policy_version>.tgz
- Contains:
  - policy/roles.yaml (default roles)
  - policy/permissions.yaml (actions/resources matrix)
  - policy/schema.json (policy schema used for validation)
  - policy/manifest.json (policy_version, bundle_build, created_at, git_sha, sha256 of each file)
  - signatures/bundle.sig (detached signature over the tarball SHA256)
- Signing is Ed25519 using minisign-compatible keys (chosen to keep verification simple in constrained / offline environments).
- Verification is performed over the tarball digest; manifest hashes provide per-file auditing/debugging.

Determinism/reproducibility:
- We normalize tar headers (uid/gid/uname/gname, file mode) and set a fixed mtime so the tarball is byte-for-byte reproducible when inputs don’t change.
- The CLI prints the computed digest and embeds the git SHA into the manifest for traceability.

CLI:
- New package: cmd/rbac-bundle
- Examples:
  - Build + sign: rbac-bundle pack --input ./policy --version v0.1.0 --out ./dist/rbac-policy-bundle-v0.1.0.tgz --sign --key ./keys/private.key
  - Verify: rbac-bundle verify --bundle ./dist/rbac-policy-bundle-v0.1.0.tgz --pubkey ./keys/public.key
  - Inspect: rbac-bundle inspect --bundle ./dist/rbac-policy-bundle-v0.1.0.tgz

Docs:
- docs/private/README.md: how policy bundles are installed and updated during upgrades, and recommended operational practices (pinning/rollback).
- docs/private/key-management.md: where the verification public key lives in Private, recommended rotation process, and what gets audited.

Notes / non-goals:
- This does not implement the installer-side integration in the Private product (that work is tracked in ENG-5388 and will consume this artifact).
- This does not add custom roles support; it only packages/ships default bundle content.

Testing:
- Unit tests cover: schema validation, manifest hashing, tar determinism, signature generation and verification, and failure modes (tampered tarball, mismatched manifest, wrong key).
- CI builds the CLI and runs pack+verify as an integration test.

Rollout considerations:
- Policy versioning is explicit (vX.Y.Z). The Private control plane should accept only “>= minimum supported bundle version” (documented), and should log policy_version and bundle digest on startup.
- If verification fails, the recommended behavior is: refuse to load the bundle and fall back to the last-known-good bundle (documented).
commits: packager: implement deterministic tar.gz builder + manifest hashing
signing: minisign (ed25519) signature wrapper + key parsing
docs(private): add upgrade/update flow and key management guidance
tests: add golden tests for determinism + signature verification
review_conversation:
Hanae Suzuki (review): Can you clarify what happens during a Private upgrade if the bundle verification fails? We should be explicit for air-gapped installs where fetching a new bundle is slow.

Fatima Noor (author): Good call. I updated docs/private/README.md to recommend “last-known-good” fallback behavior and added an explicit section on failure handling + audit logging expectations. Installer-side implementation will follow that guidance in ENG-5388.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Why minisign instead of cosign/sigstore? Also, do we have an approach for key rotation?

Fatima Noor (author): minisign is intentionally minimal (single pubkey file, no external services) and works well offline. I added docs/private/key-management.md with a rotation procedure: ship new pubkey alongside old, accept either for a window, then remove old; the manifest includes git_sha + digest to preserve traceability. We can revisit sigstore for hosted/dedicated later, but for Private/offline this seems simplest.

Connor O'Brien (review): Deterministic tarballs are great, but are we normalizing gzip headers too? I’ve been bitten by timestamps in gzip.

Fatima Noor (author): Yep. tarball.go now sets gzip.Header.ModTime to epoch and uses a stable compression level. Added a golden test that packs the same input twice and compares SHA256.

Kevin Osei (review): Please ensure the manifest contains enough info to correlate to audit logs (policy_version + bundle digest). Also, can we print reason codes on verify failure?

Fatima Noor (author): Added bundle_digest field to manifest.json and verify now returns structured errors (e.g., ERR_SIG_INVALID, ERR_MANIFEST_MISMATCH, ERR_SCHEMA_INVALID). The CLI prints a concise code + message; Private services can map those codes into audit events.

Hanae Suzuki (follow-up): docs mention public key location; can we avoid instructing customers to edit system paths by hand?

Fatima Noor (author): Updated docs to recommend installer-managed placement (e.g., /opt/redwood/etc/rbac/pubkeys/) and treating it as config managed by the upgrade process. Removed the “copy into /usr/local/share” suggestion.
release_notes: Private deployments: RBAC policy bundles can now be packaged as a signed, deterministic artifact with documented upgrade/update procedures (intended for consumption by Private installer/control plane).
